description: A thorn-racked stag so dark it reads as a gap in the wood. Violet light in its flank, and nothing regrows behind it.
lore: [[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] plants white bellflowers behind the chapel every spring, because the rite wants them and she has never found the trick of stopping. Thornstag comes in autumn, within a night or two of the same night, and takes the plot down to bare dirt. What it has browsed does not come up again — not that year, not after. She barrows the dead soil out and barrows new soil in, and she does it every time.

Inside a lamp's throw of it, which she has been, you get very little. A stag-shaped hole in the dark. A rack too wide for the gap it just came through. A violet seam working in the break of its flank, thin light where ribs ought to be. It has no interest in her whatsoever. She could put a hand on it. She has not.

[[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] sat up with her one autumn to get the thing written down and came away with three pages on the stag and nine on the bellflowers, which tells you where the story is. Everybody says fence it. Jehanne has the wood. Jehanne has had the wood four years. She stopped believing a long time ago and could not stop practising; the fires have gone out across half the map; the rota is a courtesy nobody keeps. And that stag has not missed an autumn yet. Ask her plainly and she answers plainly: she would rather be robbed on schedule than left alone.
gm_notes: Replaced the shipped line ('Corruption walking on too-long legs...'). Two reasons: 'corruption' is a genre word this setting does not use, and the art's real fact is stronger — a near-black cutout of a stag, enormous thorny rack, violet glow bleeding through a break in the haunch. Also quietly retires 'flowers die', which we do not say here. Kind is come, not hollowed: it is an animal thinned past the point of leaving anything behind it, NOT the cave's work, and it must not become a second cave-victim in the roster. Never explain the violet. Jehanne is the record — a woman who cannot pray and cannot stop gardening, whose only reliable appointment in a lapsed world is the thing that ruins her plot. If a player fences the garden for her, she will not thank them.
